candidate.answerReason: Every outer point leads to an inner point, and each inner point has two inner and two outer neighbors. After two moves, the probability of being inner is 1/2; half of that probability reaches an outer point on the third move.

methods.label: Track inner and outer points
methods.explanation:
We only need to track whether Charlotte is at an inner or outer point, because all points of the same type have the same numbers of each type of neighbor.

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

Each outer point has two neighbors, both inner. Each inner point has four neighbors: two inner and two outer. Thus, from any inner point, Charlotte has probability \(\frac12\) of moving to either type.

Charlotte starts at an outer point, so her first move certainly takes her to an inner point. After her second move, she has probability \(\frac12\) of being inner and probability \(\frac12\) of being outer.

On the third move, every route that was at an outer point moves to an inner point. Of the probability already at inner points, half moves to outer points. These two cases cover every possible route, so the requested probability is
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12=\boxed{\frac14}.
\]
The answer is \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses neighbor counts and three elementary probability updates. It requires only equally likely choices and taking one half of a fraction.

candidate.annotationRationale: The endpoint probability is found by updating the inner/outer states through the three moves. Equal neighbor counts within each type justify retaining only that state information. Graph adjacency, equally likely choices, and fraction multiplication support the written method; a general recurrence formula is unnecessary.

review.mathematicalCheck: The figure confirms that every outer point has only inner neighbors, while each inner point has two inner and two outer neighbors. The outer-point probabilities after the three moves are therefore 0, 1/2, and 1/4. Revisiting points does not affect these transitions.
